Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough this morning. Team asked for two concrete things to unblock procurement and capacity planning: a simple decomposition of our peak day into hour buckets (we call this "dayparting") and guidance on what portion of peak we should commit to vs hold back for burst/overage.

I've attached a small token sample export (aerify-token-samples.csv) and a one-pager with our internal peak-hours sketch. The most important signals: our API shows a P95 request size of ~1,250 tokens (prompt+response combined) during 14:00-17:00 PT, and we see short midday bursts where concurrency spikes 3–4x baseline for ~8–12 minutes.

Questions for Redwood:
- Do you recommend committing to sustained QPS across the full 3-hour plateau or sizing to a 30-min moving window?
- For holdback, is 25% of peak a typical starting point for auto-burst capacity in Dedicated?
- Any suggestions on model-variant fallbacks in case of quota saturation (e.g., auto-fallback to a quantized gpt-small variant)?

Appreciate a short model for committed vs holdback so procurement can draft a PO.

Best,
Samira
Samira Khan
VP, Product & Integrations
Aerify Health

Samira —

Thanks for the export and the sketch, this is exactly what we need. High level responses below and then a short set of asks so our sizing model can produce an actual GPU footprint.

Quick answers:
- Commit target: we typically recommend sizing committed capacity to the 30-minute rolling peak if latency SLOs are strict (<=200ms token compute), otherwise a 60-minute window if you can tolerate slightly higher batch-induced latency.
- Holdback: 20–30% is common. For short, sharp spikes (you said 8–12 minutes), a 25% holdback with automated burst into burstable pool + fallback routes is pragmatic.
- Fallbacks: yes — fallback to a quantized 8-bit variant is standard. We recommend 3-tier fallbacks: 1) same model lower batch size / transient queueing, 2) quantized variant with slightly lower quality, 3) feature-gated degraded response (shorter responses / truncate non-essential context).

To produce an actual GPU map we need:
1) token-level time series for at least one representative week (CSV with timestamp, requests, avg_prompt_tokens, avg_response_tokens).
2) desired P90/P99 latency SLOs and do-not-exceed P99.
3) percent of requests that require full-context (session affinity / KV cache hits matter).
4) any regulatory constraints that require Private/VPC (will affect egress and placement).

I'll pull a reference sizing model and a sample commit/holdback worksheet and send in a follow-up. If procurement needs an initial ballpark for the PO we can provide a conservative sketch within 48 hours.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Folks —

Adding a couple of operational caveats that impact GPU footprint:
- Prompt/response length distribution matters more than median. A small percent of long-horizon sessions (multi-turn summaries, 8k+ tokens) can force larger KV cache memory and reduce packing efficiency. We should get the 95th percentile of conversation length.
- Concurrency shape: if bursts are synchronized (many users at once) you need headroom on both GPU memory and vCPU for batching. If bursts are more spread (many small spikes) automated batching reduces unit cost.

Samira — can you share the P95 conversation length and an example long session (redacted)? Also tag whether any flows are streaming (server-sent events) vs single response — streaming increases socket concurrency but can lower batching efficiency.

— Ben

Samira —

Attached is a concise commitment worksheet (link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Xx_sample-daypart-report) that maps your provided daypart CSV into a starter dedicated plan. Highlights: 
- Commit to a 30-min rolling peak for the 3-hour plateau (conservative footprint: 6 x H100-equivalent GPUs with KV cache tuned for 13k token worst-case).
- Holdback plan: 25% of committed capacity reserved for bursting into a shared pool. We recommend a 2-week canary window where we monitor cache hit rates and P99 latency; if cache hits >85% and P99 < 400ms, you can reduce committed by 10%.
- Fallback ladder: quantized gpt-q8 for non-sensitive endpoints; session-truncation policy for long-running summaries.

Next steps:
1) Accept the worksheet so procurement can template a PO (we'll give line-item SKU guidance).
2) Share a weekly token-level time series for automated sizing (we can take CSV and run our sizing engine).
3) Align on SLOs (P90 latency target and P99 hard cap).

Copying Laura for procurement coordination and Karthik on deployment topology. Will spin up a detailed SKU/cost worksheet after you confirm the worksheet.

Thanks —
